posts.author: TheLivingN64
posts.body:
I'm trying to make a damage formula that increases the base damage by 0.5 for every 1% of HP lost. I've been running with the following equation, which I've tested in Python:
Code:
((120*(a.atk / b.def))+((120*(a.atk / b.def))*((a.mhp-a.hp)/a.mhp)*0.5));
Now, the issue is that it only returns 120 every time. I've realized the issue lies in the
Code:
((a.mhp-a.hp)/a.mhp)
As it only returns 0. Anything I can do?
(Also, I am aware of Yanfly Lunatic and that it has a script for this. However, that requires Lunatic damage and, considering the amount of scripts I have that interact with the damage formula box, I don't want to potentially do more damage control for just one move.

Click to expand...
Ruby automatically converts division between integers into an integer result. You'd have to cast those into decimal values.
You can instead use the built in
a.hp_rate
method.
As a side tip, it's not hurting anything but it might improve readability and reduce chances of error to not have as many superfluous parentheses.
